text: We independently test everything we recommend. When you buy through our links, we may earn a commission. Here's how we test. Our Verdict Bluehost Researched, tested and scored by The AnalyzeBench Team. See Bluehost deals → We may earn a commission · How we test Rate this post Bluehost is one of those hosting names you cannot avoid the moment you start researching how to build a WordPress site. It sits near the top of nearly every “best web host” list, it has been formally suggested on the WordPress.org hosting page for two decades, and its cartoon-friendly onboarding has walked millions of first-time website owners through their very first install. That popularity is precisely why it deserves a careful, honest look rather than the usual affiliate cheerleading. Owned by Newfold Digital (the same parent company behind HostGator), Bluehost aims squarely at beginners, bloggers, and small businesses who want a guided path into WordPress without touching a command line. In this review we walk through what Bluehost offers, what the plans really cost once the introductory pricing expires, where it shines, and where it frustrates people. We kept it balanced: real pros, real cons, no fake countdown timers. If you already know you want it, you can check current Bluehost deals and skip ahead. Otherwise, read on. AnalyzeBench Score: 8.2 / 10 Best for: Beginners and small-business owners who want the most hand-held, WordPress-friendly hosting experience and are comfortable paying a bit more at renewal for that simplicity. What we loved: Official WordPress.org recommendation dating back to 2005 — the longest-standing name on that list. Genuinely beginner-friendly setup, with one of the most guided onboarding flows in shared hosting. Free domain for the first year plus a free SSL certificate on all plans. 24/7 live chat and phone support that is always reachable. A generous 30-day money-back guarantee that lets you test risk-free. A full ladder of plans — shared, cloud, VPS, dedicated, and managed WordPress/WooCommerce — so you can grow without switching hosts. Watch out for: Renewal pricing jumps sharply after the intro term — often two to three times the promotional rate. The checkout page pre-selects paid add-ons that quietly inflate your total if you do not untick them. The cheapest promo prices usually require committing to a 36-month term up front. Raw speed is solid but not class-leading; premium managed hosts are noticeably faster. Support quality can be inconsistent during busy periods. What makes Bluehost different The single biggest thing that sets Bluehost apart is its relationship with WordPress itself. Bluehost has appeared on the official WordPress.org list of recommended hosts since 2005, making it the longest-running name there. As of this writing it is one of only a small handful of companies WordPress.org names alongside providers like Hostinger and Pressable. That endorsement is a real signal — WordPress does not hand it out casually — though it is fair to note the arrangement is also a commercial partnership, not a purely neutral technical award. Treat it as meaningful but not gospel. Beyond the badge, Bluehost’s identity is built around removing friction for beginners. When you sign up, it does not drop you into a bare control panel and wish you luck. Instead it walks you through picking or migrating a WordPress site, choosing a theme, and getting the basics configured, all through a guided wizard. For someone who has never touched hosting before, that difference is enormous. Many competitors assume a baseline of technical comfort that Bluehost simply does not require. The trade-off is that this beginner focus comes bundled with an aggressive commercial layer: checkout upsells, prominent promo pricing, and renewal rates much higher than the headline number. None of that is unusual for shared hosting, but Bluehost leans into it more than some rivals. Knowing this going in is the key to good value, which is why we cover it below. The core service At its heart, Bluehost is a managed and shared web host optimized for WordPress. Every plan includes a free SSL certificate, a custom control panel layered on top of the familiar cPanel-style tools, automatic WordPress installation, and a free domain name for the first year. You also get email hosting, one-click staging on higher tiers, automated daily or scheduled backups depending on plan, and a content delivery network to help with global load times. The dashboard is where Bluehost’s beginner-first philosophy shows. Rather than throwing dozens of icons at you, it surfaces the handful of things a new site owner needs: create a site, manage a domain, check email, view performance. WordPress-specific features like staging, one-click plugin and theme management, and automatic core updates are woven into the interface, so you rarely leave the Bluehost panel to run a WordPress site. Security is handled with free SSL across the board, malware scanning on appropriate tiers, and optional add-ons like CodeGuard backups and domain privacy. Some extras are genuinely useful; others are the same pre-ticked upsells we keep warning about. The core hosting stack is capable and well-suited to the small-to-medium WordPress sites that make up most of Bluehost’s customer base. If that describes you, Bluehost’s current plans are worth a look. Bluehost dashboard Hosting plans & pricing Bluehost offers a full ladder of hosting types, so most users can start small and move up without changing providers. Prices below reflect the general structure at the time of writing; always confirm the live figure on Bluehost’s site before you buy, because promotions shift and the exact number depends on the term length you choose. The headline pattern to remember: introductory rates are low, and renewal rates are meaningfully higher. Shared hosting This is the entry point and where most first-time site owners begin. Shared plans run across several tiers, from a basic single-site Starter plan up to plans that allow unlimited websites, more storage, and extra performance features. Introductory pricing is aggressive — often in the low single digits per month — but that rate typically requires a 36-month commitment, and it climbs substantially at renewal. Shared hosting is ideal for blogs, portfolios, and small business sites that are not yet pushing heavy traffic. Managed WordPress hosting For those who want WordPress handled for them — automatic updates, tuned performance, staging, and WordPress-specific support — Bluehost’s managed WordPress plans add a layer of convenience on top of the shared foundation. This is a sensible middle ground for people who take their WordPress site seriously but do not want to become server administrators. WooCommerce hosting Aimed at online stores, the WooCommerce plans bundle the ecommerce plugin plus store-oriented features like inventory management, gift cards, and shipping-label printing. These tiers are priced above standard shared hosting and are designed to support stores handling meaningful monthly visitor volumes. If you are launching a shop rather than a blog, this is the tier to compare. Cloud hosting Bluehost’s cloud offering targets sites that have outgrown shared resources and want better reliability, with an emphasis on high uptime and stronger performance. Cloud plans sit at a notably higher monthly price than shared hosting, reflecting the additional resources and resilience on offer. VPS hosting Virtual private server plans give you isolated, dedicated resources — guaranteed RAM, CPU allocation, and room to scale — for sites that have pushed past what shared hosting comfortably handles. VPS pricing is well above shared hosting because you are paying for isolation and predictable performance rather than a shared pool. Dedicated hosting At the top of the ladder, dedicated servers give you an entire physical machine. This is for large, high-traffic, or resource-hungry sites that need maximum control and performance. It is the most expensive option by a wide margin and is overkill for the average user, but it means you never have to leave the Bluehost ecosystem as you grow. How to get the best deal (watch renewals) This is the most important section of the review, so read it before you check out. Bluehost’s advertised prices are genuine, but they are introductory rates available to new customers for the initial term only. When that term ends, the plan renews automatically at the regular rate, which is often two to three times the promotional price. This is standard practice across the shared-hosting industry, but the size of the jump surprises people who did not read the fine print. A few practical tips to get the most out of a Bluehost purchase: Understand the renewal math. A promo price that looks cheaper than a rival may cost more over three years once renewal kicks in. Calculate the full multi-year total, not just the first year. Choose your term deliberately. The lowest monthly promo rate usually requires a 36-month prepayment. That locks in the low rate for longer, but it is a larger upfront commitment. A 12-month term costs a bit more per month but ties up less cash. Untick the add-ons at checkout. Bluehost pre-selects extras like site backups, domain privacy, and security tools. Some are worthwhile, but they are opt-out, not opt-in. Review each line before paying. Use the money-back guarantee. The 30-day window is real. If the service does not suit you, you can request a refund on the hosting portion within that period. Consider paying annually and renewing manually. Some users prefer shorter terms so they can reassess — and potentially negotiate or switch — rather than auto-renewing at full price for three years. Handled thoughtfully, Bluehost can be very good value, especially for a first site. The people who feel burned are almost always the ones who did not realize the renewal rate was coming. You can see the latest Bluehost pricing and read the term details directly before committing. Watch: Bluehost in action If you would rather see the signup and dashboard experience before reading further, this hands-on review walks through what actually using Bluehost feels like, including an honest take on the pricing and the upsells. Bluehost vs alternatives No host is right for everyone. Here is how Bluehost stacks up against two of the most common alternatives people weigh it against: Hostinger, the budget champion, and SiteGround, the performance-and-support favorite. Feature Bluehost Hostinger SiteGround Best for Beginners wanting guided WordPress setup Lowest long-term price Speed and premium support WordPress.org recommended Yes (since 2005) Yes Formerly listed Intro pricing Low, term-dependent Lowest of the three Higher Renewal pricing Jumps significantly Also jumps, but lower base Jumps the most Raw speed Solid Solid to strong Class-leading Support reputation Good, occasionally inconsistent Good Excellent Free domain (year 1) Yes On longer terms No The short version: Hostinger tends to win on pure long-term cost, SiteGround tends to win on speed and support polish, and Bluehost wins on the beginner experience and the depth of its WordPress integration. If you value being guided through your first site over squeezing out the last dollar or millisecond, Bluehost is a strong pick. Bluehost pricing and plans Uptime, speed & value Bluehost advertises a 99.99% uptime target, and independent testing generally backs that up, with reviewers reporting uptime in the high 99.9% range and only brief, infrequent outages. For a shared host, that is dependable and well within the range you would expect for typical small-business and blog workloads. Speed is the more nuanced story. In testing, Bluehost consistently loads well-optimized sample sites quickly and handles moderate traffic spikes without collapsing. Measured time-to-first-byte and page load times are perfectly adequate for small to medium sites, but they trail the fastest premium managed hosts. In plain terms: your visitors will not sit around waiting, but if raw speed is your single top priority, a specialized managed host will edge Bluehost out. On value, the honest answer depends on the renewal math. During the introductory term, Bluehost is genuinely affordable, especially with the free domain and SSL included. Over multiple years at renewal rates it moves into mid-market territory — you are paying for ease of use and WordPress integration, not rock-bottom pricing. Who should use it — and who should not Bluehost is a great fit if you are: a first-time website owner who wants the most hand-held path to a live WordPress site; a small business or blogger who values simplicity and 24/7 support over squeezing out maximum performance; or someone who wants a single provider they can grow with, from a shared plan up to VPS or dedicated over time. The guided setup alone saves beginners hours of frustration. Bluehost is probably not for you if you are: a performance-obsessed developer who needs the fastest possible load times and is willing to manage more of the stack yourself; a bargain hunter focused purely on the lowest three-year cost, where a rival like Hostinger often wins; or an experienced sysadmin who finds the guided, upsell-heavy interface more of an obstacle than a help. Power users sometimes feel boxed in by the beginner-oriented panel. Honest limits To keep this balanced, here are the caveats we would want a friend to know. First, renewal pricing is the number one source of buyer’s remorse; the headline rate is not what you pay long term. Second, the checkout flow pre-checks paid add-ons, so an inattentive buyer can pay more than intended. Third, Bluehost was historically known for migration fees and for support that varies with queue volume; onboarding and migration tools have improved over time, but support consistency remains a fair concern at this scale. Finally, being part of a large conglomerate means Bluehost optimizes for the mainstream beginner, which is why advanced users sometimes feel constrained. None are dealbreakers for the target audience, but they are real. Bluehost discount codes & deals Bluehost runs promotional pricing more or less continuously, so there is rarely a need to hunt for a separate coupon code — the introductory discount is usually baked into the signup price you see. The best “deal” is simply choosing the right term for your situation and remembering to untick the add-ons you do not need at checkout. Because Bluehost includes a 30-day money-back guarantee, you can sign up, build your site, and test the service with very little risk. If it is not the right fit, request a refund within that window — a fair way to try before you commit. Frequently asked questions Is Bluehost really recommended by WordPress? Yes. Bluehost has been on the official WordPress.org list of recommended hosts since 2005 and is the longest-standing name there. It is worth understanding that this is both a technical endorsement and a commercial partnership, so treat it as a strong positive signal rather than an absolute guarantee that it is the single best host for your specific needs. Why is the renewal price so much higher than the intro price? The advertised low price is an introductory rate for new customers, valid for the initial term only. When that term ends, the plan renews automatically at Bluehost’s standard rate, which is often two to three times the promo price. This is common across the shared-hosting industry; the key is to calculate your true multi-year cost before signing up. Does Bluehost include a free domain? Yes, most Bluehost plans include a free domain name for the first year, along with a free SSL certificate. After the first year the domain renews at its standard registration rate, so factor that into your ongoing costs. Is Bluehost good for beginners? This is arguably Bluehost’s strongest selling point. Its guided onboarding walks you through creating or migrating a WordPress site, choosing a theme, and configuring the basics, all without touching a command line. If you have never built a website before, this hand-held experience is one of the best in the industry. Can I get a refund if I do not like it? Yes. Bluehost offers a 30-day money-back guarantee on hosting. If you cancel within that window you can get a refund on the hosting portion of your purchase. Note that domain registration fees are typically non-refundable once the domain is registered. Is Bluehost fast enough for my site? For blogs, small business sites, and most WordPress projects, yes — Bluehost delivers dependable uptime and load times that keep visitors happy. For large or performance-critical sites, consider a premium managed host or Bluehost’s higher tiers like VPS, cloud, or dedicated. How to choose a web host (a quick education) If you are new to all this, here is a compact framework for choosing any web host. Use it to sanity-check whether Bluehost or a rival is right for you. Match the host to your project. A personal blog, a business site, and a busy online store have very different needs. Do not overpay for VPS or dedicated resources you will not use, and do not cram a high-traffic store onto an entry-level shared plan. Read the renewal price, not just the intro price. This is the single most common trap. Always calculate the total cost over the full period you expect to stay, using the renewal rate. Check uptime and speed reputation. Look for hosts with a solid uptime guarantee (99.9% or better) and independent speed testing, rather than relying only on marketing claims. Value real support. When your site goes down, responsive 24/7 support matters more than almost anything else. Beginners in particular should weight this heavily. Look for a money-back guarantee. A genuine refund window lets you test the service in practice with little risk, which is far more reliable than any review, including this one. Plan for growth. Choose a provider whose plan ladder lets you scale up without migrating to a whole new host later. Measured against that checklist, Bluehost scores well on beginner-friendliness, support availability, WordPress integration, and its growth path, while asking you to stay alert on renewal pricing and checkout upsells. For a huge share of first-time site owners, that is a very reasonable trade. If it sounds like the right fit, you can check current Bluehost deals and get started with the 30-day guarantee behind you. Rupee billing with UPI makes checkout easy for Indian buyers, though the renewal jump and lack of a local data center are worth weighing first. 9.6 Key Features Guided WordPress-first onboarding wizard cPanel access alongside Bluehost's own dashboard Free WordPress migration tool Free SSL certificate (Let's Encrypt) on every plan Weekly automated backups Staging environments to test changes safely Built-in Yoast SEO (free version) Malware scanning and removal (Business and above) WooCommerce tools for online stores 24/7 live chat, with phone support on Business and eCommerce plans Overview If you've spent any time researching web hosting, you've probably run into Bluehost more than once. It's one of the oldest names in the business, started back in 2003 in Provo, Utah, and it's still one of the few hosts that WordPress.org itself points beginners toward. That endorsement isn't just a badge on a website; it means Bluehost's servers are genuinely built with WordPress in mind, and it shows the moment you sign up. The setup experience is where Bluehost earns most of its reputation. Instead of dropping you into a control panel and leaving you to figure things out, it asks a few simple questions, what kind of site you're building, whether it's a blog, a business page or a store, and walks you straight into a working WordPress dashboard. For someone building their first website, that's a genuinely useful head start. For Indian users specifically, Bluehost runs a dedicated Bluehost setup, which means you're not stuck converting dollars in your head or hunting for an international card. Prices show up in rupees, and you can pay with UPI, a debit card, or net banking, the way you'd expect from a service actually built for the Indian market, not just translated for it. Where it's a bit more old-fashioned is support. Bluehost still offers phone support, something most modern hosts have quietly dropped in favour of chat and AI assistants. If you're the sort of person who'd rather talk something through than type it out, that alone might be worth the extra cost over cheaper competitors. The trade-off is that Bluehost doesn't have a data center in India, so if most of your visitors are local, your site may load a touch slower than it would on a host with servers here. Pricing follows the pattern most hosts use now: a low rate to get you in the door on a long-term plan, followed by a noticeably higher renewal rate once that term ends. It's not hidden or deceptive, it's just something to plan for rather than be surprised by two or three years down the line. Overall, Bluehost feels like a dependable, if slightly traditional, choice. It's not chasing the lowest price on the market, and it's not trying to be the flashiest dashboard around. What it offers instead is a stable, well-documented, WordPress-first experience with a real person on the phone if you need one, which, for a lot of first-time website owners, is worth more than shaving off a few hundred rupees a month. How BlueHost Works Bluehost is an American hosting company, founded in 2003 in Utah and now part of the Newfold Digital group. You pick a plan, pay upfront for 12 or 36 months, and your site is ready shortly after. It's built around WordPress: the signup flow asks what kind of site you want (blog, business, portfolio, store) and walks you straight into a working WordPress dashboard, no separate installation step needed. Everything is managed through the Bluehost account panel, plus standard cPanel access underneath for anyone who wants it. That combination, a guided setup layered over a familiar control panel, is what earned Bluehost its long-standing recommendation from WordPress.org itself. A note for Indian buyers: unlike Hostinger, which prices and bills natively in rupees with UPI support, Bluehost prices in USD and India-facing checkout typically shows an INR conversion at the live exchange rate. The rupee figures in this review are approximate conversions, not a fixed rupee price. Confirm the exact amount at checkout. Collaboration Tools Bluehost supports multiple websites and multi-site management from a single account on Business and eCommerce plans, with staging environments so you can test changes before publishing. There’s no dedicated “invite a collaborator” flow like Hostinger’s Account Sharing – team and client access is generally managed via cPanel user accounts or directly sharing WordPress logins. Visit Site → Data Privacy & Security Every plan includes free SSL and weekly backups. Business and eCommerce plans add malware scanning and removal, and domain privacy for the first year. Bluehost also runs its Security tab for IP blocking, hotlink protection and WordPress core file checks. Daily backups and stronger malware tools are part of an optional Security Bundle add-on rather than included by default on the entry plan, unlike Hostinger where daily backups come with the mid-tier plan itself. BlueHost Customer Support This is where Bluehost stands out from budget hosts like Hostinger: 24/7 phone support is available (on Business and above; Starter gets chat only), alongside live chat and a large knowledge base. That's genuinely useful if you'd rather talk to a person than a chatbot. That said, user reviews are inconsistent: some praise fast, knowledgeable agents, others report long holds and unhelpful chat bots before reaching a human. Live chat usually asks a few automated questions before connecting you to someone. BlueHost Pricing How Much Does BlueHost Cost? Bluehost offers three main shared hosting plans, billed natively in Indian Rupees on the longest term, 36 months, which gets you the lowest monthly rate. The Starter plan starts at around ₹330 a month, suited to a single simple website or blog, with 10 websites' worth of room (up to 10 sites), 10 GB of NVMe storage, a free domain for the first year and weekly backups. Step up to Business (Choice Plus) at around ₹580 a month, and you get 50 websites, 50 GB of storage, plus malware scanning, domain privacy and, importantly, 24/7 phone support alongside live chat, something the Starter plan doesn't include. At the top, eCommerce Essentials costs around ₹1,245 a month and adds WooCommerce built in, 100 GB of storage and support for up to 100 websites, aimed at anyone planning to sell online. All three plans come with free SSL, a free domain for the first year, a 99.99% uptime SLA and a 30-day money-back guarantee, and you can pay through UPI, debit or credit cards, net banking or digital wallets since Bluehost is set up for Indian customers. The catch is renewal. Once your 36-month term ends, prices jump substantially, Starter renews at roughly ₹830 a month and eCommerce Essentials at around ₹1,825, so what looks like a bargain upfront costs noticeably more from year four onward. It's still reasonable value, especially with phone support included on the higher tiers, but it's worth budgeting for that renewal rather than being surprised by it. As with any promotional pricing, confirm the exact current rate on Bluehost's site before you buy, since offers and exchange-rate-linked figures shift over time. If your visitors are mostly local and price matters more to you than having a phone line to call, Hostinger is probably the more sensible switch. What you give up is Bluehost's phone support and its long-standing WordPress.org endorsement. SiteGround SiteGround is the one to look at if performance and support quality matter more than saving money. It runs on Google Cloud infrastructure, and its uptime and speed numbers consistently beat both Bluehost and Hostinger in independent tests. The trade-off is price: SiteGround's renewal rates are some of the steepest in the industry, so you're paying for that extra polish. Cloudways Cloudways is a different category altogether. It's managed cloud hosting rather than shared hosting, meaning your site gets dedicated resources instead of sharing a server with hundreds of others. It's the pick for a site that's outgrown shared hosting, a busy store, a client site, anything where performance under load actually matters. It costs more upfront, but there's no renewal shock the way there is with Bluehost or Hostinger, since the price you pay is the price you keep paying. DreamHost DreamHost is worth a mention mainly because it's the other host WordPress.org officially recommends alongside Bluehost. It backs that up with a 100% uptime guarantee, which is a bold promise few hosts are willing to make. If Bluehost's WordPress pedigree is what drew you in, DreamHost gives you that same credibility with a different pricing structure. GoDaddy GoDaddy rounds out the list mostly on brand recognition. Almost everyone's heard of it, and it bundles domains, hosting and marketing tools in one place, which some people find convenient. It's not usually anyone's top pick on pure hosting quality, but if you'd rather manage everything, domain, email, hosting, through one familiar company, it's a reasonable option. If you're choosing between these mainly because of Bluehost's India-specific drawbacks, the honest short version is this: Hostinger solves the price and location problem, SiteGround solves the performance problem, and Cloudways solves the scale problem. Pick based on which one is actually bothering you, rather than switching just because a list told you to. But in our tests, we noted it falls short in performance and also lacks many features that are standard with our top hosts . Overall, it’s a mixed bag, but it might still be the host for you. Touted as one of the “top hosting services worldwide,” it’s maintained a certain golden status for years. It’s especially popular with first-time bloggers and small e-commerce site owners who are drawn to its generous first-term discounts and simple, beginner-friendly interface. Few review sites properly test Bluehost’s service, though. I mean, how can you honestly recommend a service that you haven’t even tried out? We did test it, measuring every aspect of hosting a WordPress site using Bluehost – from ease of setup to its uptime rate, page loading speeds, and even how well the support team… well, supports. Key takeaways? For ease of use, Bluehost’s sleek control panel and fast sign-up process excelled. The support team was also very responsive and helpful. However, performance was a major letdown . And although very affordable when signing up, Bluehost’s hosting renewal rates typically double. I also found the features and “freebies” included in its plans are easy to beat if you shop around for another host. If you’re skeptical about Bluehost but still want to weigh the pros and cons, this review is for you. I suggest you also take a look at our round-up of the top 10 best web hosting services to see how Bluehost compares to other highly rated hosts. 3.5 Features Considering Yoast is owned by the same company as Bluehost, a free paid Yoast plan would have been nice Many “Free” Features – Which Are Generally Free Anyway Features add value to a hosting package, but Bluehost may have taken marketing its “extras” too far. The host makes a big deal of certain features being “free,” but this is misleading since you can use these services and plugins for free no matter which hosting provider you’re with. Naturally, first-time website owners won’t know any better. For example, the “Bluehost WordPress Marketplace” is very similar to the actual WordPress Marketplace . It features a selection of curated free and premium WordPress and WooCommerce themes and plugins. The only difference is that you access them directly via the Bluehost admin panel instead of in the WordPress dashboard. Likewise, the included “Yoast SEO Free” is just the free version of this popular WordPress SEO plugin. While this integration makes sense considering both Bluehost and Yoast are subsidiaries of Newfold Digital, surely a premium tier plan for Yoast could be included for free instead? Discover More Bluehost Features >> Multi-Site Plans The entry-level shared and WordPress plans from Bluehost allow for 10 websites. The three more expensive ones let you host 50–100 websites. If you only plan to create one website, the Basic hosting package storage limitation of 10GB shouldn’t be too much of an issue. However, issues may arise if you want to create and manage multiple sites on one of Bluehost’s plans. Mainly, you’ll want to keep an eye on the amount of storage you have remaining, especially if your sites have a lot of large images or other storage-intensive media files . If you’re hosting text-based blogs, though, the 50–100 GB of space on the top-tier plans should be more than enough for a lot of smaller sites. If you’re looking to have no such limits on storage, IONOS’s Plus hosting plan with unlimited storage , bandwidth, and websites might be a better fit. Even better, this plan costs less than Bluehost’s equivalent mid-tier plan after renewal. SSL Certificates & More (Paid) Security Features In addition to a year of domain name registration, you can expect a number of other add-ons – such as integration with Cloudflare’s CDN and SSL certificates. The SSL certificates are the standard ones from Let’s Encrypt , which are intended to provide a very basic level of SSL encryption . In other words, it removes the “not secure” warning and adds a padlock icon to the address bar in web browsers when people visit your site. Paying for backups should never be an option as far as hosting goes Though affordable, you’ll note that Bluehost’s cheaper Basic and Plus plans don’t come with any more security features than the above, though . In comparison, the premium Choice Plus and Pro shared hosting plans include domain privacy and daily website back-ups – but, disappointingly, only for your first year. After years of reviewing web hosts, paying for backups should never be standard. Bluehost may have other redeeming qualities, but if you want free security, Hostinger offers free and on-demand backups on both shared and cloud hosting plans – and it’s still cheaper than Bluehost. After signing up, you can purchase various paid add-ons from the Bluehost Marketplace to ramp up your security. For a fee, you can add a Single Domain SSL and SiteLock Security , which includes the use of the much more secure TrueSpeed CDN and the TrueShield firewall. Though they are affordable, you’ll note that Bluehost’s Basic hosting plans don’t come with more security features than the above. In comparison, every premium WordPress and shared hosting plan from Bluehost comes with domain privacy, malware scanning, and daily website back-ups included. A Free Domain Name One value-for-money extra Bluehost includes in its plans is a free domain name. It’s a handy addition if you’re looking to bundle all of your website launch costs into one. Keep in mind that a domain name is never truly “free” as fees must be paid to the organizations that oversee the domain name system – so, if you decide Bluehost’s services aren’t for you, and you decide to take advantage of Bluehost’s 30-day money-back guarantee, the cost of the domain name will be subtracted from your refund . You can then take the domain name with you to a new provider. Bluehost Features at a Glance Free domain name ✔ Free backups ✘ (1 year of free daily backups on top-tier plans) Free email ✘ (only 3-month Pro Email trial) Money-back guarantee 30-day money-back guarantee Uptime guarantee Partial – 100% SLA on cloud plans only Data centers Orem, Utah (US) 4.7 Ease of use My Hosting Experience With Bluehost There’s nothing complicated about the Bluehost hosting admin panel – and that’s a good thing I did appreciate the speed and simplicity of getting started with Bluehost . Featuring a two-step order process, WordPress auto-installer, and an automatic site creation and optimization questionnaire, getting my website up and running was very straightforward. The Bluehost admin panel was equally delightful to navigate after I signed up. Though it did take a bit of time for certain pages to load, the layout is clean, uncluttered, and made sense. Creating a New Account With Bluehost Bluehost’s streamlined sign-up process has no painfully drawn-out marketing and upselling – I only hade to navigate domain setup and payment. I was also be prompted to pay and create my Bluehost account and login credentials simultaneously. The typical account creation details required on the payment page itself included my name, address, and contact details. The account creation tool also allowed me to specify my chosen service term and paid hosting add-ons. That said, I recommend thoroughly reviewing all of these, as some paid extras are pre-selected . For example, the Professional Email free trial was pre-selected, and if you don’t cancel it, it renews at full price after the 3 months is up. You’ll be prompted to create your Bluehost account during payment It’s nice that Bluehost’s accepted payment methods include a number of cards, such as Visa, MasterCard, Discover, and American Express. It also accepts PayPal, money orders, and checks. Additionally, all shared Bluehost plans also come with a $100 Google Ads and Bing Ads credit . However, you won’t see this offer listed on your order summary itself and for Google Ads, you’ll need to spend a minimum of $25 on your existing account to claim your credit. Connecting a Domain and Installing WordPress After payment for my Bluehost hosting plan was complete, I could focus on setting up my website. Handily, the domain name setup page pops up just before the payment page. Bluehost’s free domain selection includes a decent range of domain extensions You can select your free domain from a number of popular domain extensions or add an existing domain, if needed. The inclusion of many popular US, UK, and global domain extensions in Bluehost’s free domain name selection is definitely a win. You can choose one that best fits your unique demographic and audience instead of settling for a generic one. Whether you take advantage of Bluehost’s free domain offer or use your own, Bluehost will point the DNS for you. Once my account was set up, it was time to install WordPress with Bluehost’s 1-click WordPress installer. Under the Websites tab in my account panel, I clicked on Add First Website . From here, you can choose between installing WordPress or transferring an existing WordPress site. If you choose the fresh WordPress install, you’ll need to add your site title and link it to a domain name. Once you click Continue , your WordPress install should begin. The process only takes a few minutes. You’ll need to log into your WordPress admin dashboard to edit your site, which you can do via the Bluehost panel. Overall, it’s a super straightforward, stress-free process. If you can’t find your way around, there are also plenty of self-help guides and tutorials available. Other Ease-of-Use Features Easy Access to WordPress From Your Control Panel Jump straight to your site’s WordPress Dashboard via the Bluehost admin panel Once WordPress is set up, you can also log in password-free from your Bluehost admin panel. As a WordPress-forward host, Bluehost offers a lot more features for the popular CMS, too. For example, you’ll have access to a WordPress site migration tool and a WordPress AI site builder. Do note that – as with many providers – Bluehost’s shared and WordPress hosting plans are essentially the same products with different names. If you sign up for a regular web hosting plan, you can still install WordPress. Custom Bluehost Admin Panel & WordPress Dashboard Manage your WordPress website from your Bluehost admin panel – and vice versa Bluehost’s admin panel and your WordPress Dashboard are somewhat linked on its WordPress hosting plans. You can publish and edit website content directly from the Bluehost admin panel, or use exclusive Bluehost tools from your WordPress Dashboard. This feature is useful if you’re new to WordPress hosting as it allows you to edit your website content from your Bluehost panel. Google My Business Setup Bluehost offers integration with Google My Business, allowing you to seamlessly connect your site and a Google Business account together. This way, you can get your business listed and mapped out on Google Maps in one place – a nice touch, particularly for those with physical stores or offices. 3.9 Performance Adequate Performance – But Mainly in the US Bluehosts’ main demographic is US-based sites and audiences. A contributing factor is that Bluehost’s data centers are located in Utah , meaning Bluehost-hosted sites perform best here and in nearby states and countries like Canada. These are the assumptions you’d have when signing up to Bluehost, right? But when I ran my tests , my Bluehost-hosted WordPress site scored somewhat poorly for performance in the US . With a typical page loading time of about 2 seconds or more, I can’t recommend it at all. Loading speeds were inconsistent overall, regularly dipping to 1.2 seconds and jumping up to over 4.5 seconds over the course of just 24 hours. And, though Bluehost’s uptime was reliable at 100%, it’s not backed by a guarantee unless you buy a cloud plan. GTmetrix Performance Tests My Bluehost test site typically took over 2 seconds to load – which is just over the edge of acceptability according to the majority of hosting experts. However, there were many deviations throughout the day and week, with my site frequently taking well over 3 seconds to load . This is one of the main reasons I just can’t recommend Bluehost, and also why many customers have left the host. Bluehost’s performance was less than impressive in GTmetrix tests It’s very difficult to attribute deviations to peak times as performance seemed to ebb and flow throughout the week. But if you think this is normal for a budget host, it’s not. For example, Hostinger offers plans for cheaper (before and after renewal), but consistently served loading speeds of around 1 second or less in our tests for exactly the same test site. In a one-week period, Bluehost’s performance wavered drastically The primary problem was identified in the Time to First Byte measure. Once the testing server in Chicago was able to make that first connection with the data center in Utah, page assets would often load in less than a second . But it would frequently take more than a second – sometimes more than two – for the Time to First Byte connection to take place. Keep in mind that this was the default setup for a Bluehost hosting plan , and with various plugins and other tweaks, it could be better. However, we try to test a hosting plan without these performance tools active to see what you’ll get out of the box. Sucuri Load Time Tester Global Speeds Bluehost is highly recommended for US & UK audiences – but less so further afield From my Sucuri Load Time Tester results, you can see that US-based connections – particularly on the West Coast, near Bluehost’s Utah-based data centers – performed the best . At around half a second or less for a full page load, these speeds are higher than average. Server connections as far away as London and the Netherlands performed well, too. Other regions showed mixed results. To be fair, servers in some of these locations – particularly France and Germany – may have blocked the Sucuri Load Time Tester connection. UptimeRobot Bluehost’s reliability rate was quite impressive In my UptimeRobot tests, my website averaged a 100% uptime rate over the course of a month . My site only dropped out for a short 3-minute period during this time, which may be attributed to Bluehost’s regular maintenance. If you’re wondering if Bluehost compensates for downtime, here’s the deal: Bluehost only has a proper service-level agreement (SLA) in place for its cloud plans . It guarantees 100% uptime for your hosted site and compensation if terms aren’t met. While there’s also a 99.9% uptime for VPS and dedicated plans, I couldn’t find any legal documentation to back this up in its Terms & Conditions. There’s absolutely no SLA for shared plans. Instead, Bluehost’s Network Server Uptime Agreement lists the likelihood of downtime for server maintenance and measures taken to restore your site. If a server goes down, Bluehost claims that most fixes take approximately 15 minutes to a day or more (in extreme cases). And, no, you won’t be compensated for any unexpected downtime. Despite stellar UptimeRobot results, I can’t say I find this lack of accountability reassuring. You shouldn’t have to worry about server outages and the potential financial losses these could cause your business. There are definitely better hosts to go with if you need an iron-clad SLA. For example, HostArmada will credit 10% per hour up to 100% of your monthly fee for any downtime – and this is applicable for its shared hosting plans. 4.7 Support Bluehost support is available 24/7 via phone and live chat Solid 24/7 Support – Via Phone & Live Chat Bluehost has a streamlined support offering , with agents available via phone and live chat 24/7. You can also consult the knowledge base on the Bluehost website, which is filled with helpful articles on many relevant topics. The level of support I received from Bluehost was more than satisfactory. When reaching out to Bluehost through live chat, there were some small problems. Mostly, the Bluehost chat representative was slow to respond at first, taking a minute or longer to answer each message at the start of the chat. However, he quickly caught up, so I might have just got him at a bad or busy time – I did make contact at around 4:00 p.m. MT on Sunday afternoon. A bit slow to hop on board, but Bluehost support was helpful and fast thereafter When I called Bluehost phone support, the phone tree directed me to where I needed to go immediately. Once I was connected to a Bluehost support agent, they were on in less than a single ring and very helpful and friendly . Even better, the agent asked for a verification token instead of a portion of my Bluehost account password – a less-than-safe practice it’s been found guilty of in the past. 4.5 Pricing Very Affordable Until the Discounted First Term Runs Out Bluehost certainly falls in the category of budget hosting, offering amazingly low rates . However, if you plan on staying longer than the initial discounted first term, be prepared for a cost increase. That said, its renewal rates are still quite low, and you can find deals and coupons to reduce the price further. . Save up to 75 % on your Bluehost plan! Get Deal In terms of value for money, one issue with Bluehost’s hosting plans is their limited capabilities and the lack of truly valuable included features. Most of the “freebies” – such as Cloudflare CDN, Yoast SEO Free, Let’s Encrypt SSL certificates, and WordPress plugins and themes – are free anyway. And others, like domain privacy and daily backups, are only free on the priciest plans for one year. Both Bluehost basic and premium plans also include less storage and fewer security and performance features than many similarly-priced competitor hosting plans. With this in mind, it may be worth your while to compare a few other hosting providers before you sign up. FAQ Does the free domain name provided by Bluehost belong to me? Yes, the free domain name included with Bluehost web hosting packages does belong to you. In fact, if you cancel your Bluehost hosting plan, you still retain ownership of the domain name for the full term for which it’s registered. Thereafter, you’ll need to renew it to retain ownership of it. You can use it for any website – whether hosted by Bluehost or built on WordPress or not. Do Bluehost web hosting plans include webmail hosting? Most Bluehost hosting plans allow you to create and manage email accounts as long as they are associated with your registered or linked domain name. You can also sign up for a Google Workspace account with Bluehost if you need something more professional. These paid plans include access to advanced Google email management tools. Do I need to pay for Bluehost web hosting if I have WordPress? WordPress.com allows you to create and host a WordPress website on WordPress servers. This is different from installing the free WordPress.org software on Bluehost’s server – this is often referred to as “self-hosted” WordPress, and it gives you more customization options. Can I transfer my website to Bluehost? If you have an existing WordPress website, you can migrate it to Bluehost during WordPress setup . If you’re moving your site while still on contract, you may also qualify for a credit, but you need to contact Bluehost first to apply. Migration of non-WordPress sites will cost you extra (around $149.99). How does Bluehost compare to Hostinger? Bluehost and Hostinger may seem quite similar. For starters, they both offer WordPress-friendly shared plans, an AI site builder, and budget pricing. However, there are differences that make Hostinger the better option , including better performance and features. Hostinger’s shared plans also offer LiteSpeed servers, weekly or daily backups, and advanced security solutions. Are there hosts with better performance and uptime than Bluehost? Yes, there are many hosts that offer better performance than Bluehost. One contributing factor to Bluehost’s unreliable performance is its limited data center locations. text: Bluehost is one of the biggest web hosting companies in the world and an official WordPress-recommended hosting provider since 2005. But if you’re like most smart people, you don’t make decisions based on endorsements. You want to do your research and see how Bluehost compares to others in the market with real speed test results. In July 2026, I tested Bluehost the same way I tested 14 other WordPress hosting companies , with an identical WordPress site on a custom domain, the same tools, and the same checklist. This Bluehost review will show you the real numbers from my rigorous speed test using industry-standard benchmarking tools. Quick Answer – Is Bluehost Worth It? Yes, Bluehost is worth it if you are a beginner who’s looking to start a website. It scored 69 out of 100 on our WPBeginner Score, which places it 6th out of our 7 recommended hosts. In our hosting speed test, Bluehost performed well and the website loaded with a 933 ms LCP (Largest content paint). It is one of the easiest hosts to start with, and WordPress.org has recommended it longer than any other host. Their entry plan allows you to host up to 10 websites for $2.99 per month, and you get a free domain for the first year. It’s a great pick if you’re launching your first website, blog, or a small online store. However if your priority is raw speed and you have a high traffic eCommerce website, then you may want to look at a more managed WordPress hosting provider like Levamo . Bluehost at a Glance Bluehost Test Summary (July 2026) WPBeginner Score 69 / 100 Speed (LCP) 933 ms Global response time 599 ms average across 6 regions Uptime 100% over a 30-day monitoring window Pricing From $2.99/mo with our link, renews at $9.99/mo Support 24/7 live chat and “Ask Blu” AI assistant (no phone support on the entry plan) Best for Beginners building their first website You can see how Bluehost ranks against all the hosts I tested in our best WordPress hosting comparison, which uses the same data as this review. About Bluehost Bluehost started in 2003 and now powers more than 5 million websites. It has been on WordPress.org’s recommended hosting list since 2005, longer than any other company. While the official WordPress endorsement matters, I did not let it influence my review. The verdict below comes from what my hosting speed test actually measured. Pros and Cons of Bluehost Pros Officially recommended by WordPress.org since 2005 Simplest setup of any host I tested – Bluehost installs WordPress for you at signup 10 websites, 10 GB NVMe storage, a free CDN, and AI setup tools on the $2.99 entry plan – most hosts at this price allow one site Staging, SSH access, and object caching included on every plan – features some hosts save for higher tiers Reasonable renewal at $9.99 per month, with a free domain for the first year 100% uptime during our 30-day monitoring window Cons Slower speed than many other hosts we tested – 933 ms LCP, where the fastest host we tested loaded in 358 ms Weekly backups only, where DreamHost includes daily backups at a lower price No phone support and no domain privacy on the entry plan Aggressive upsells during signup – you can uncheck them, but you have to pay attention Several “free” extras convert to paid after the first year or first month (more details in the fine print section below) How I Tested Bluehost (Methodology) I used the same testing protocol for every hosting company in our comparison. I set up an identical WordPress site with a default theme and test content, including images, on a custom domain with no caching plugins. Then I ran the same four tests – GTmetrix for speed and LCP, k6 for stress with 50 virtual users at the same time, a response-time test from 6 global regions, and 30 days of Uptime Robot monitoring. Those four tests make up the performance side of the WPBeginner Score, which counts for 80% of the total. Each test carries a set weight, so no single lucky number can carry a host. The other 20% of the score comes from value. For that part I look at what the plan really costs and gives you in return – the intro price, the renewal price, how many sites and how much storage you get, the plan limits, and the quality of support. The full methodology, the exact weights, and every host’s raw numbers are in our best WordPress hosting guide. Bluehost Performance Test Results Below you can find my full Bluehost speed test results. Speed Test – 933 ms LCP Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) measures how quickly the main content of a page appears. It is the speed number Google’s Core Web Vitals care about most. My Bluehost test site showed an LCP of 933 ms, and the full page loaded in the same time. I will be honest about this number. Under one second load time is fine for a starter site with no optimization. However, when I tested other popular hosts, the median LCP was 659 ms, and the fastest hosting company, Levamo , loaded in 358 ms. If raw speed is your top priority, Bluehost is not the winner on our data. Server Response Time – 599 ms Global Average Speed test tools load the whole page with images included, but that’s only one part of the performance. To see raw server speed, I also measured time to first byte (TTFB) from data centers in 6 regions around the world. Bluehost averaged 599 ms across the 6 regions. Response times were good in North America and most regions. South America and Japan were noticeably slower. Our test site ran in Bluehost’s default US location, so this pattern makes sense. If your audience is mostly in the US, then Bluehost speed will be just fine for you. If your audience is global, then make sure to turn on the included Cloudflare CDN. It serves your content from locations closer to your visitors. Stress Test – Blocked by Cloudflare Protection To see how a host behaves under a traffic spike, I send 50 virtual users to the test site with k6 by Grafana Labs and record the P95 response time. When I ran this on Bluehost’s test site in our latest round, the test could not complete. Bluehost’s built-in Cloudflare integration flagged the synthetic traffic as an attack and blocked it, even after allow-listing. Our last completed stress run on Bluehost held a 140 ms P95 at 50 concurrent users, with no failed requests. The block itself has an upside. The same protection that stopped my load test is what stands between your site and a real DDoS attack. But it also means I cannot give you a current under-load number for Bluehost server, and I would rather tell you that than pretend otherwise. Uptime – 100% Over 30 Days I monitored the Bluehost test site with UptimeRobot, checking every 5 minutes. Over the 30-day window, it recorded 100% uptime with no incidents. Bluehost also guarantee their shared hosting with a 99.99% uptime SLA. The fine print is worth knowing because if uptime falls below that, then you can claim a single 5% monthly credit, and you must claim it within 30 days. In our monitoring window, Bluehost stayed above its own promise. How Bluehost Compares to Other Hosts We Tested The speed test numbers on their own do not give you the full picture. Here is how Bluehost performed compared to other similarly priced hosts from our comparison, all tested with the identical setup. Host LCP Global response Uptime Intro / renewal WPBeginner Score Bluehost 933 ms 599 ms 100% $2.99 / $9.99 69 / 100 Hostinger 659 ms 227 ms 100% $2.69 / $10.99 88 / 100 SiteGround 608 ms 369 ms 99.96% $2.99 / $17.99 75 / 100 DreamHost 986 ms 658 ms 100% $1.99 / $7.99 64 / 100 The WPBeginner Score weighs performance at 80% and value at 20%. Bluehost’s 69 reflects exactly what you see above – it trails on speed and response time, while its value for a beginner is strong (10 websites where most entry plans give you one). To see the full rankings, and the raw data for every host we tested, check out our best WordPress hosting guide. Bluehost’s Infrastructure and Technology Most other Bluehost reviews skip what’s under the hood on their shared hosting platform, and I believe it’s worth highlighting. Storage and caching – every plan runs on NVMe SSD storage, which is the faster generation of SSD. You also get two caching layers included, static content caching and object caching, on every plan. Some hosts charge extra for object caching, so seeing it in the $2.99 plan at Bluehost is a genuine plus. Data centers – Bluehost recently migrated to the Oracle Cloud data centers which offer state of the art infrastructure. Bluehost allows you to choose from different data center locations across North America, South America, Europe, and Asia during checkout. I recommend choosing the one closest to your audience. CDN and security – free Cloudflare CDN comes with every plan, along with free SSL from Let’s Encrypt and malware scanning. The Business plan and higher add an extra web application firewall and DDoS protection. Developer and maintenance tools – every plan includes SSH and WP-CLI access, a one-click WordPress staging site, and managed WordPress updates. Bluehost keeps your WordPress core updated for you, which removes a maintenance task most beginners forget. Bluehost Hosting Plans and Pricing Bluehost offers shared, VPS, dedicated, cloud, and WooCommerce hosting. For most readers of this review, the shared WordPress plans are the relevant ones. Starter – 10 websites, 10 GB NVMe storage, 5 email accounts, and capacity Bluehost rates at around 40,000 visits a month. $2.99 per month for the first term with our link, renews at $9.99 per month. Staging, SSH, and object caching are included even here. Business – 50 websites, 50 GB NVMe storage, unlimited email accounts, and capacity for around 200,000 visits a month. Starts at $5.99 per month, renews at $13.99. This tier adds phone support, a web application firewall, DDoS protection, and free domain privacy for the first year. eCommerce Essentials – 100 websites, 100 GB storage, and capacity for around 400,000 visits a month. Starts at $13.99 per month, renews at $21.99. It auto-installs WooCommerce and bundles commerce add-ons – subscriptions, memberships, paid courses, an affiliate program, and one-click checkout – that would cost real money as separate plugins. All plans include a free domain for the first year, free SSL, the Cloudflare CDN, malware scanning, the free Yoast SEO plugin, free WPForms plugin, and weekly backups. All plans also come with a 30-day money-back guarantee. In my experience, a new site will not outgrow the Starter plan for a long time for most small business use-cases. You can move to the Business plan when you need phone support, domain privacy, or the firewall, and pick eCommerce Essentials only if you are building an online store on day one. Free and Paid Hosting Addons Bluehost’s headline price is honest, but several extras start free and quietly become paid. Knowing these up front will save you surprise charges. Free domain – free for the first year on 12 or 36-month terms, and you must claim it within 90 days. After year one it renews at the standard domain rate. If you cancel hosting within the 30-day guarantee window, Bluehost deducts a non-refundable domain fee from your refund. This is fairly standard practice across all shared hosts that offer a free domain. Professional Email – a one-month free trial that auto-renews at $2.99 per month unless you cancel. Your 5 included cPanel email accounts on Starter are separate and stay free. Domain privacy – free for the first year on Business and up. Starter does not include it at all, so your registration details are public unless you pay for it. SiteLock and CodeGuard – paid add-ons Bluehost offers for extra security and backups. The included malware scanning and weekly backups cover the basics, so skip these at signup and add them later if you need them. Refund rules – the money-back guarantee covers hosting only, runs for 30 days, and excludes add-ons like domains. Bluehost gives no refunds after day 30. Bluehost for WordPress Beginners This is where Bluehost really stands out. When you create a Bluehost account, they install WordPress by default, so there is no setup step to get wrong. The custom dashboard is the clearest I have used on a budget host. Websites, email, domains, and security sit in one place, and cPanel is still there for advanced tasks like databases. Bluehost has also added AI site creation tools and AI agents that help you build and manage your website. I would treat these as a convenience rather than a reason to choose a host, but for a first-timer they remove real friction. Bluehost Customer Support Bluehost offers 24/7 live chat, a large knowledge base with step-by-step guides and videos, and an AI assistant called “Ask Blu” that handles common questions instantly. The entry plan does not include phone support, so chat is your only option if you start on the Starter plan. There is also no ticket system, so an issue that needs multiple sessions means re-explaining it in chat. To be fair, phone support is rare at budget hosting prices, and most hosts at this level stick to chat. Bluehost adds phone on the Business plan or higher. Of all the budget hosts that we tested, SiteGround was one of the few that included phone support on every plan. Who Should Use Bluehost and Who Should Look Elsewhere Choose Bluehost if you are building your first website, blog, or small business site and want the simplest possible start. The official WordPress.org recommendation, the automatic install, and 10 websites on the cheapest plan make it the lowest-friction way in. Its 100% uptime in our monitoring backs the reliability claim. Look elsewhere if raw speed is your priority, since Hostinger and SiteGround both beat Bluehost by a wide margin in our tests. The same goes if you want daily backups on a budget (DreamHost includes them at $1.99), need phone support on an entry plan (SiteGround), or run a high-traffic site that needs proven performance under load (try Levamo and see our full hosting comparison ). Final Verdict – Is Bluehost the Right Choice for You? Bluehost is perfect for beginners who are just starting out or someone building a small business website. They’re officially recommended by WordPress.org which is a big endorsement. My verdict – if this is your first website, visit Bluehost and start on the Starter plan. If speed is your deciding factor or you have outgrown your first site, our best WordPress hosting comparison shows which host won each category on the same tests. FAQs About Bluehost 1. What are the disadvantages of Bluehost? Based on our tests, the main ones are speed (933 ms LCP, not as fast as others that we tested), weekly rather than daily backups, no phone support or domain privacy on the entry plan, and upsells during signup. Several free extras also convert to paid after the first year, which the fine print section above covers. 2. Is Bluehost good for beginners? Yes. This is actually where Bluehost really stands out. Bluehost installs WordPress for you at signup, the dashboard is simple, and 24/7 live chat is there when you get stuck. It is the host we recommend most often to someone building their first site. 3. Can Bluehost handle high traffic? Bluehost rates the Starter plan for around 40,000 visits per month, which covers most new sites comfortably. In our last completed stress test, Bluehost held a 140 ms P95 response with 50 concurrent users and no failures. Bluehost’s own Cloudflare protection blocked our most recent re-test, so we could not measure its current under-load behavior. For consistently high-traffic or eCommerce sites, a managed host is the safer pick. 4. Can I make an online store with WooCommerce on Bluehost? Yes. The eCommerce Essentials plan auto-installs WooCommerce and includes premium commerce add-ons like subscriptions, memberships, and one-click checkout. For a new store with modest traffic it works well. As your store grows, plan to upgrade, because stores are harder on a server than blogs. 5. Is Bluehost better than GoDaddy? For WordPress, I believe Bluehost is definitely better than GoDaddy. Bluehost’s onboarding and dashboard are more beginner-friendly, and its pricing is clearer for small sites. We have not run GoDaddy through our new speed test protocol, so I will not compare speed numbers until we have, but based on my historical experience, I am pretty confident in my answer. 6. How does Bluehost compare with SiteGround and Hostinger? On our identical tests, both SiteGround and Hostinger were faster. SiteGround loaded in 608 ms and Hostinger in 659 ms, against Bluehost’s 933 ms. Bluehost counters with the simplest setup and 10 websites on its entry plan. SiteGround costs more at renewal ($17.99 per month), and Hostinger also skips phone support. The comparison table above has the full numbers, and our SiteGround vs Bluehost comparison goes deeper. 7. Where are Bluehost’s servers located? Bluehost recently moved to Oracle Cloud, and they now offer server locations across North America, South America, Europe, and Asia that you pick at checkout. Our test site ran in the default US location, which is why our North American response times were strong while Japan and South America lagged. The included CDN closes most of that gap for global audiences. 8. Which Bluehost plan should I get? We recommend starting with their Starter plan . It covers 10 websites and roughly 40,000 monthly visits, which is more than a new site needs. Upgrading later takes a few clicks, so there is no reason to overbuy on day one.
